explanation.whyCorrect: The brick states loperamide inhibits acetylcholine and prostaglandin release, reducing peristalsis to increase water absorption from stool, and increases anal sphincter tone to decrease urgency.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Blocking 5-HT3 receptors describes alosetron.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Binding bile acids describes bile-acid sequestrants.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Stimulating prostaglandin and mucus secretion describes bismuth subsalicylate's mucosal defense action.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Increasing chloride secretion describes IBS-C drugs like lubiprostone, which promote diarrhea, not treat it.

questions.topicName: Laxatives and Antidiarrheals
questions.stem: A 38-year-old man is prescribed a combination antidiarrheal containing diphenoxylate and atropine. Which of the following best explains why atropine is included in this formulation?

choices.label: C
choices.text: To reduce the risk of pancreatitis

choices.label: D
choices.text: To discourage misuse and dose escalation

explanation.summary: Diphenoxylate crosses the blood-brain barrier and can cause CNS effects, so atropine is added; its unpleasant anticholinergic effects at higher doses discourage dose increases and misuse.
explanation.whyCorrect: The brick states diphenoxylate crosses the blood-brain barrier leading to CNS effects, so it is combined with atropine to dissuade dose increases, with anticholinergic side effects occurring in excess.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Atropine is added to deter overuse, not to boost antidiarrheal potency.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Fat-soluble vitamin deficiency relates to bile-acid sequestrants, not this combination.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Pancreatitis risk relates to eluxadoline, not diphenoxylate-atropine.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Atropine is an antimuscarinic, not a serotonin receptor blocker.

questions.topicName: Laxatives and Antidiarrheals
questions.stem: A 25-year-old man plans international travel and wants to prevent traveler's diarrhea. He is advised to take bismuth subsalicylate. Which of the following best describes how this agent works?

choices.label: A
choices.text: It enhances mucosal defense and binds enterotoxins

choices.label: B
choices.text: It binds bile acids that cause colonic secretion

choices.label: C
choices.text: It antagonizes mu-opioid receptors in the gut

choices.label: D
choices.text: It activates guanylate cyclase C on the epithelium

choices.label: E
choices.text: It lowers the surface tension of the stool

explanation.summary: Bismuth subsalicylate enhances mucosal defense (stimulating prostaglandin, mucus, and bicarbonate secretion), inhibits intestinal prostaglandin synthesis and chloride secretion, and has direct antimicrobial activity while binding enterotoxins, making it useful for traveler's diarrhea.
explanation.whyCorrect: The brick states bismuth subsalicylate enhances mucosal defense, exhibits direct antimicrobial activity, and binds enterotoxins, contributing to its effectiveness in preventing and treating traveler's diarrhea.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Binding bile acids describes bile-acid sequestrants such as cholestyramine.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Antagonizing mu-opioid receptors describes opiate antagonists like methylnaltrexone.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Activating guanylate cyclase C describes linaclotide, an IBS-C drug.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Lowering stool surface tension describes the emollient docusate.

questions.topicName: Laxatives and Antidiarrheals
questions.stem: A 44-year-old woman with diarrhea-predominant IBS and hyperlipidemia is treated off-label with cholestyramine, which improves her diarrhea. Which of the following is the main adverse effect associated with this drug?

explanation.summary: The main adverse effect of bile-acid sequestrants such as cholestyramine is interference with the absorption of other drugs and of fat-soluble vitamins in the GI tract.
explanation.whyCorrect: The brick states the main adverse effect of bile-acid sequestrants is interference with the absorption of drugs and fat-soluble vitamins in the GI tract.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Ischemic colitis is the rare serious adverse effect of alosetron.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Melanosis coli is caused by chronic senna use.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Pancreatitis is associated with eluxadoline.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Urinary retention and dry mouth are anticholinergic effects of atropine.

questions.topicName: Laxatives and Antidiarrheals
questions.stem: A 52-year-old woman with severe, refractory diarrhea-predominant IBS is being considered for alosetron. Which of the following serious adverse effects most limits the use of this drug?

explanation.summary: Alosetron is reserved for women with severe or refractory IBS-D partly because of a rare but serious risk of ischemic colitis that can require transfusion, surgery, or even cause death.
explanation.whyCorrect: The brick states alosetron carries a rare but serious risk of ischemic colitis, which may result in a need for blood transfusion or surgery, or even death, limiting its use to severe or refractory cases.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Pancreatitis is the serious adverse effect of eluxadoline, not alosetron.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Xerostomia is an anticholinergic effect of atropine combined with diphenoxylate.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Melanosis coli results from chronic stimulant laxative use.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Flatulence is the adverse effect of bulk-forming laxatives, not a serious limiting effect of alosetron.

questions.topicName: Laxatives and Antidiarrheals
questions.stem: A 46-year-old man with diarrhea-predominant IBS is being considered for eluxadoline. Which of the following patients would this drug be contraindicated in?

choices.label: A
choices.text: A patient with a history of asthma

explanation.summary: Eluxadoline increases the risk of pancreatitis from sphincter of Oddi spasm and is contraindicated in patients who have had a cholecystectomy.
explanation.whyCorrect: The brick states eluxadoline is contraindicated in patients who have had a cholecystectomy because of increased risk of pancreatitis due to sphincter of Oddi spasm.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Asthma is not listed as a contraindication to eluxadoline in this brick.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Hypertension is not a stated contraindication to eluxadoline.
whyWrongByChoice.D: An ileostomy is actually a setting where antidiarrheals may be used, not a contraindication to eluxadoline.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Age over 65 is not a stated contraindication; prior cholecystectomy is.

questions.topicName: Laxatives and Antidiarrheals
questions.stem: A medical student is reviewing laxative classes. Which of the following agents is classified as a bulk-forming laxative?

explanation.summary: Psyllium, bran, and methylcellulose are the bulk-forming laxatives; they absorb water and distend the intestine to trigger peristalsis.
explanation.whyCorrect: The brick lists psyllium, bran, and methylcellulose as examples of bulk-forming laxatives.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Docusate is an emollient (stool surfactant).
whyWrongByChoice.B: Senna is a stimulant (cathartic) laxative.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Lactulose is an osmotic laxative.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Bisacodyl is a stimulant laxative.

questions.topicName: Laxatives and Antidiarrheals
questions.stem: A 68-year-old man takes a magnesium-containing laxative for constipation. In addition to its osmotic effect, this agent increases intestinal motility partly by stimulating release of which of the following hormones?

explanation.summary: Magnesium-containing laxatives may stimulate release of cholecystokinin (CCK), leading to intraluminal fluid and electrolyte accumulation and increased intestinal motility.
explanation.whyCorrect: The brick states magnesium-containing laxatives may stimulate the release of cholecystokinin (CCK), which leads to intraluminal fluid and electrolyte accumulation and increased intestinal motility.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Gastrin drives gastric acid secretion and is not the hormone stimulated by magnesium laxatives here.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Secretin stimulates pancreatic bicarbonate and is not implicated in this brick's mechanism.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Somatostatin inhibits GI secretion and motility, the opposite of the described effect.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Vasoactive intestinal peptide drives intestinal secretion but is not the hormone stimulated by magnesium laxatives here.
